newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end higher on firmer beef outlook.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end higher on firmer beef outlook.

text.p: Fund short covering and commercial support kept CME live cattle futures strong at the close despite a sharp setback in neighboring pork complex pits, traders said.

Live cattle futures appeared oversold, after recent losses pushed the Relative Strength Index into the 20s. That, coupled with light commercial interest and a lack of outside selling, rallied the market, traders said.
Perceptions that beef values may be near a bottom and recent brisk packer buying of cash cattle earlier in the week than expected, reinforced gains.
Also, retailers are expected to feature beef early in November before poultry takes over for the holidays, sources said.
"Apparently, there is talk packers picked up right away the cattle they bought this week which would indicate they have beef business," said Jim Clarkson, analyst for A and A Inc.

December also appeared oversold based on price projections going into the end of the year but traders were cautious with the USDA Cattle-on-Feed report due out Friday. The report will give the market a more definite direction, traders said.

Estimates for October 1 seven-state on-feed cattle supplies at major feedlots in Friday's monthly report averaged 94.8 percent of a year ago and ranged from 93.8 to 97 percent. However, September placement estimates averaged 98.6 percent in a range of 96.2 to 104 percent of a year ago when placements were historically large. Marketing estimates averaged 87.8 percent in a range of 85 to 90.8 percent.
In live cattle options, there was wire house put selling in February through June strikes late, pit sources said.
Feeder cattle futures followed the lead of live cattle with lower corn futures also prompting demand, traders said.

Commercials tried to do feed margins all day, buying feeder cattle and selling live cattle, but selling interest was lacking with fed cattle markets likely firming soon and feed costs continuing to ease.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.13 at $62.85 per cwt.
Feeder cattle futures closed up 0.875 to 0.200 cent with October up 0.675 cent at 63.175 cents a lb and November up most at 63.450 cents per lb.
Live cattle ended up 0.575 cent to off 0.125 with only distant October off and December up 0.550 at 65.275 cents.
